key_insight: The paper explains spectral bias through the eigenvalue decay and eigenvector shapes of a graded dynamics matrix, linking learning order to sinusoidal components.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a theoretical lens for understanding how activation choices influence which signal components a neural network learns first.
method: Expand network outputs as a general Fourier series in an orthogonal polynomial basis.
Express gradient-descent coefficient dynamics as ordinary differential equations governed by a matrix H.
Analyze H using its graded structure and orthogonal polynomial theory.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical analysis rather than datasets, benchmarks, or quantitative experimental results.
watch_item: Applicability to arbitrary architectures remains a goal; the abstract does not establish practical predictive accuracy beyond the shallow-network setting.
paper_title: Why Shallow Neural Networks Learn Sinusoidal Components First: An Orthogonal Polynomial Dynamics Framework
